newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alleged Port Arthur gunman arrives at court.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Port Arthur gunman arrives at court.

text.p: The man accused of committing the worst mass killing in modern Australian history arrived at a court in Tasmania on Monday to enter a plea to 35 charges of murder.
Martin Bryant, 29, arrived at the Supreme Court of Tasmania in Hobart in a prison van with black windows.
Security was exceptionally tight with the road in front of the court blocked off by police in both directions.
Bryant's hearing was due to start at 10 a.m. (midnight GMT).
If Bryant pleads guilty, he is expected to be remanded until Thursday to hear submissions on sentencing.
On April 28, a sunny Sunday afternoon, a lone gunman walked into the Broad Arrow Cafe at the Port Arthur historic site and shot 20 people as they ate their lunch.
Within an hour a further 12 people, including a three-year-old girl, were gunned down either outside the cafe, in their cars, or hiding behind a tree.
Three people were taken hostage and later found dead in the charred remains of a cottage near the former penal colony.
Bryant faces a total of 70 charges, including 35 of murder and 19 of attempted murder.
